Micro food-resilience

How well nearby farms could feed a balanced, diverse diet. Click anywhere on the map.

Click the map to score a location.

How the score works

Each farm's acres are split among its crops and converted to an estimated yearly harvest of protein, carbohydrate and fat, expressed as person-years: the number of people that nutrient could fully cover for a year at FDA Daily Values (50 g protein, 275 g carbs, 78 g fat per day).

Farms within the radius count toward a point, weighted by distance (a Gaussian falloff: a farm at half the radius counts ~61%, at the edge ~14%).

Sufficiency = 1 − e−min(P, C, F) / people. The scarcest macronutrient sets it, so a place rich in fat but short on protein scores low.

Diversity uses the effective number of foods D (exp of Shannon entropy over calorie shares). Factor = (1 − w) + w·(1 − 1/D).

Score = 100 × sufficiency × diversity. Yields are rough regional defaults; calibrate them against the County Crop Report before drawing conclusions. Livestock, eggs, dairy and fish are not modeled.
